summary: Implemented the provider-neutral single-subject publication orchestration and the single Jellyfin image-mutation implementation in src/ArrTags/Artwork, driving the authoritative durable publication protocol (docs/architecture.md section 9 steps 4-10; ADR-002, ADR-003; docs/data-model.md 3.10.1-3.10.4) through the confirmed Jellyfin 12.0.0 ABI. IArtworkImageWriter is the host-neutral mutation boundary; JellyfinArtworkImageWriter is its only implementation and resolves the item through ILibraryManager, calls the supported IProviderManager.SaveImage(BaseItem, Stream, string, ImageType, int?, CancellationToken) stream overload with the durable derived bytes and image/png, then calls BaseItem.UpdateToRepositoryAsync(ItemUpdateType.ImageUpdate, ...), matching the standard item-image controller. It never writes a media-folder poster, Jellyfin's image cache, or an item-image path directly, never uses the filesystem-path overload that deletes its source, and never uses a URL overload; all MediaBrowser.* references for publication are confined to that one file and src/ArrTags/Rendering stays Jellyfin-free. ArtworkPublisher reads the authoritative PublishedArtworkState, observes and confines the current source through IArtworkSourceReader, retains a present baseline (or records an explicit absent baseline) in the task 5.2 SourceArtifactStore, promotes the validated render output to a durable derived artifact (bounded by OperationalLimits.DerivedArtifactLimitBytes and verified against RenderResult.OutputHash), builds the exact expectedBeforeIdentity from a fresh source read and the candidateAfterContentSha256 from the derived artifact, and writes a Prepared ArtworkOperation before any external image mutation. It re-reads and revalidates the before identity immediately before mutation; a mismatch or unobservable identity never calls SaveImage and marks the operation Aborted. When a previously published session exists, the failed check also persists the ownership outcome (OwnershipLost/OwnershipUnknown); when no prior publication session exists (an initial capture), the failed check persists no PublishedArtworkState. It durably advances through MutationStarted, RepositoryUpdateStarted, VerificationPending, and FinalizationPending before each external step, reads back the effective active image, and commits the final PublishedArtworkState (new publication token, active identity, state revision, and lastOperationId while retaining the source artifact and ownership token) before marking the operation Committed. Any failure or uncertainty leaves the current artwork unchanged, records a bounded non-secret diagnostic, and never marks the operation committed; a pre-existing non-terminal or recovery-blocked operation (and invalid/quarantined state or journal) blocks new work. Repeat publication verifies the prior publication is still active, reuses the first source artifact and ownership token, issues a new publication token, and never captures an ArrTags output as a new source. The publisher is registered with the existing lazy factory DI pattern and performs no startup work; no event, queue, or library-scan wiring is added (Phase 6 drives the single entry point).

known_limitations: The Jellyfin stream SaveImage overload has no saveLocallyWithMedia parameter; Jellyfin's ImageSaver chooses the destination from the library's own SaveLocalMetadata option and may therefore store the published bytes in the media folder through its supported API. ArrTags does not select or write that path directly and never uses the filesystem-path overload (which deletes its source), so this is Jellyfin's supported behavior rather than a direct media-folder or cache write. This boundary is recorded in docs/architecture.md section 9 and docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 4.4.

The publisher performs the normal publication path only; it records uncertainty as RecoveryBlocked (or an Aborted no-mutation outcome) but does not implement the task 5.7 recovery/reconciliation decision table, restart reconciliation, or lifecycle fencing (5.9). A pre-existing non-terminal or recovery-blocked operation deliberately blocks new automatic publication for that subject until reconciliation exists.

In-process per-subject serialization uses a static ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> that is never pruned. It is bounded by the number of distinct published item/surface subjects and is safe (the durable generation fence remains the authority), but the dictionary and semaphores are not reclaimed during the process lifetime.

Derived artifacts are promoted through the same SourceArtifactStore as source artifacts, so SourceArtifactStore.Promote additionally enforces OperationalLimits.SourceArtifactLimitBytes on the derived bytes. An over-limit derived image is therefore rejected before any mutation (DerivedArtifactRejected, no durable operation and no Jellyfin call): the publisher first enforces DerivedArtifactLimitBytes, then the shared store enforces SourceArtifactLimitBytes, so the effective derived bound is the smaller of the two. This is fail-closed and cannot produce a false commit or a readback-time uncertainty; no unconditional limit-order validation was added because it would change the accepted OperationalLimits contract.

Derived artifacts are stored in the same content-addressed SourceArtifactStore (and manifest kind) as retained source artifacts, as the task directs. Reference-proven cleanup/retention of derived versus source artifacts remains the task 5.7 retention/reconciliation work.

No live Jellyfin host run and no real library mutation were performed; all coverage uses injectable IArtworkSourceReader/IArtworkImageWriter doubles and DispatchProxy doubles for ILibraryManager/IProviderManager. Live end-to-end standard-route delivery remains task 5.11.

Item-type eligibility (Movie/Episode only) is not enforced by the publisher or the source adapter; the V1 surface is enforced and item-type eligibility remains the caller's concern (as already documented for task 5.3), to be applied by the Phase 6 pipeline.
